hero.title:
Retro gaming,
built Linux first.
hero.lede: OpenEmux wraps the power of RetroArch in a clean GNOME-native frontend — so you can browse your collection with cover art, pick up a gamepad, and just play. No config files. No setup rabbit holes. Linux is where it is designed, built and tested first; Windows runs the same app, in beta.
hero.note: Free and open source · MIT licensed · AppImage, .deb, .rpm & Flatpak on Linux · installer & portable ZIP on Windows
hero.shot_alt: alt="OpenEmux library view showing SNES games with cover art" />
features.title: Emulation without the homework
features.lede: RetroArch is one of the most powerful emulation platforms ever built. OpenEmux gives it an interface that gets out of your way.
features.shelf:
A real game shelf

Your library, organized by console with full cover art synced automatically from the libretro thumbnail archive.
features.first_boot:
Zero-config first boot

On first launch OpenEmux sets up its config and downloads the cores your consoles need, in about ten seconds. The rest arrive in the background while you browse.
features.controls:
Per-console controls

Map keyboard and gamepad inputs per system in a friendly panel. Bindings are injected into RetroArch at launch time.
features.shaders:
Shaders that look right

Pick a CRT or scanline shader per console from a curated catalog and it just applies — no shader menu spelunking.
features.native:
Linux first

Built in GTK4 and Adwaita, following the GNOME HIG, and tested on Linux before anything else. Linux is a first-class citizen here; Windows comes along, in beta.
features.bios:
BIOS at a glance

A clear checklist of which BIOS files each console needs and which ones you already have. No more silent launch failures.
philosophy.title: Play the games you own
philosophy.lede: OpenEmux is a front-end for RetroArch, built to make emulation approachable. It is not a source of games — it ships no games, no ROMs, no BIOS files, and never will.
philosophy.own: • Use only content you legally own. Dump your own cartridges and discs, or use backups of games you purchased.
philosophy.piracy: • Piracy isn't what this is for. Downloading copyrighted games you don't own is illegal in most countries.
philosophy.history: • Emulation preserves history. So much of gaming's art, music and design lives on fragile aging hardware. Keeping it playable is legitimate — and it works best when it respects the people who made these games.
systems.title: Four decades of consoles, one library
systems.lede: Nintendo, Sega, Sony, Atari and more — each with its own cores, cover art, input profiles and shader settings.
shots.title: Your collection, on a shelf
shots.lede: Cover art, organized by console — the way a game library should look. Scroll through the systems, and click any shot to view it full-size.
shots.settings_lede: ROM paths, BIOS checks, input mappings and shaders — all in one clean panel, no config files.
install.title: Running in under a minute
install.lede: Grab a package for your distro, the universal AppImage, the Flatpak — or, on Windows, the installer. OpenEmux handles the rest on first launch.
install.flatpak_note: Updates arrive with flatpak update. A single-file .flatpak bundle is on the Releases page too.
install.windows_lede: Both builds carry GTK 4, the Python runtime and RetroArch itself, so there is nothing to install alongside them. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. It is new — if something misbehaves, open an issue.
install.installer_note: Installs for your user only, so no administrator prompt. The builds are not code-signed yet: SmartScreen will warn, and More info → Run anyway gets past it.
install.portable_note: Unzip it anywhere and run OpenEmux.exe from the OpenEmux\ folder inside. Good for a USB stick or a machine you cannot install software on.
install.verify_lede: Every release ships a SHA256SUMS file. Put it next to the artifact you downloaded and run:
install.verify_ok: OK means the file is exactly what was published. Anything else means it is corrupt or tampered with — don't run it.
install.verify_windows: On Windows, PowerShell prints the hash and you compare it by eye with the matching line in SHA256SUMS:
install.build: Prefer building it yourself? make bootstrap && make run — see the build instructions.
thanks.title: Thanks to RetroArch, libretro & OpenEmu
thanks.lede: OpenEmux was directly inspired by OpenEmu, the beloved macOS emulator that made retro gaming feel effortless and beautiful. Since OpenEmu is macOS-only, OpenEmux exists to bring that same polish to Linux first, and now to Windows too. None of it would be possible without the incredible work of the RetroArch and libretro teams. ❤️
support.title: OpenEmux is free — and stays free
support.lede: If it made your retro shelf a little nicer, consider buying me a coffee. It helps me keep improving features and stability. And come say hi on r/OpenEmux — share your setup, ask for help, or follow what's coming next.
